capabilities: Edit notes collaboratively with per-user cursors and selections
Leave anchored comments, replies, and mentions with an activity feed
Synchronize open and closed notes, renames, and deletions with the server
Assign folder-level roles for editors, commenters, and viewers
Keep local version snapshots and reconcile disk conflicts
disambiguation: Not a mood or journaling tracker; it is a client for real-time multi-user editing of notes on a shared server.
extras: Requires an organization-run server; the repo contains only the Obsidian client while the server source is private. Warns that stored credentials sit in plain plugin data and that 'stay signed in' should not be used on shared devices. Security issues are reported privately via SECURITY.md.
problem: Obsidian vaults are local single-user files with no built-in way for multiple people to edit the same note together or discuss changes in place.

requires.name: account on a compatible Mood Collab server

summary: Real-time collaboration client that lets teammates co-edit Markdown notes with shared cursors, comments, presence, and server-based sync.
